newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian mineral sector supports budget basics.
newsitem.headline: Australian mineral sector supports budget basics.

text.p: Australia's Federal 1997/98 budget should contribute to a more secure basis for the country's economic future, Dick Wells, executive director of the Mineral Council of Australia, said on Tuesday.
This would be achieved by continuing the focus on economic fundamentals and a fiscal strategy of returning the budget to underlying surplus by 1998/99, he said in a statement.
"(But) the way in which this is achieved is of critical importance," Wells said.

Fiscal/monetary policy measures must be directed to maximising growth of the national economy and be complemented by continuing and accelerating microeconomic reform to improve Australia's international competitiveness, he said.
In the medium-term it was imperative that the government effectively address land access issues and progress debate on taxation reform, he said.
The decision to abandon the second tranche of legislated tax cuts in favour of measures to stimulate savings was welcomed, he said.
The minerals sector welcomed the government's commitment to the retention of the diesel fuel rebate scheme and the research and development tax incentive, he said.
"Any change to the rebate scheme would represent a punitive tax on the mining industry and on Australia's major export earners," he said.
